transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-15 14:30 PDT — Duration ~48 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Ethan Chen (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Hightower — Head of ML Infra), Connor Lee (Hightower — Platform Eng), Aisha Khan (Hightower — InfoSec)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
- Hightower evaluating Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU capacity) for customer-facing LLM features and bulk embedding jobs.
- Key constraints: data isolation (no shared multi-tenant GPUs), compliance (SOC2/ISO, KMS/HSM), predictable latency during market hours, and ability to burst for peak loads.
- Next steps: pricing, security pack, benchmark run, deep-dive.

00:00 Sofia: ok everyone, thanks for joining, i'll kick us off — this is Sofia from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account, with Ethan our solutions engineer.
00:08 Maya: hi Sofia, thanks, i'm Maya, i'll run infra here, Connor and Aisha are with me.
00:12 Connor: hey all.
00:20 Ethan: great, quick agenda — understand your workloads, sizing and SLA needs, security requirements, and talk about dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs and burst strategy. sound good?
00:30 Maya: yeah that's perfect. we did a proof of concept with hosted initially but ran into noisy-neighbor stuff and variable tail latency during peak trading windows, so we want to look at dedicated/reserved.
00:44 Sofia: totally, that's exactly why Dedicated exists. quick question — what's your rough concurrency/throughput today for the customer-facing chat vs batch embedding jobs?
00:55 Maya: chat is around 150 concurrent sessions during the morning peak, average prompt size small (50-120 tokens). we see p95 latency spikes to 600-800ms on hosted during peaks which is unacceptable. embeddings are bulk — nightly jobs, about 2M documents a week currently.
01:12 Ethan: ok good data — for dedicated we typically size by peak concurrent and expected qps, plus embedding throughput. do you have a preferred latency SLO?
01:20 Connor: target would be p95 < 200ms for short prompts and steady throughput during the 9-11am window; we can accept higher latency for longer prompts or non-real-time workloads.
01:32 Aisha: security side — we need strict data isolation, keys managed with our KMS/HSM, audit logs, and SSO/SAML integration. also retention rules for logs and model inputs.
01:45 Ethan: that's all supported — Dedicated gives single-tenant pools, private control plane options, and we integrate with customer KMS for key wrapping. audit logs and long-term retention are part of the enterprise pack. we'll share the security pack.
01:58 Maya: good. can you outline how burst capacity works? we have unpredictable spikes — e.g., earnings season spikes where traffic can 3-4x for a few hours.
02:12 Sofia: yes. Dedicated has reserved base capacity plus optional burst policies that can draw from shared cloud pools or pre-warmed burst nodes. bursts can be configured with max cap and fallback policies. in practice we recommend a commit for base plus a configured burst limit to avoid cold starts.
02:31 Ethan: technically we support two burst strategies — on-demand cloud burst (faster for short spikes but at higher unit cost) and scheduled pre-warmed nodes (lower cost but needs lead time). both can be configured with routing policies so critical traffic uses reserved nodes first.
02:50 Connor: what about scaling speed? if we hit a sudden 3x demand, how quickly do new GPUs come online?
02:59 Ethan: for on-demand cloud burst we can spin up instances within ~3-8 minutes depending on instance type and region; pre-warmed nodes are instant. we also do continuous batching and KV cache reuse to smooth token throughput which helps reduce required GPUs. so sizing plus batching gives you better effective throughput.
03:20 Aisha: you mentioned private control plane — does that mean traffic stays in our VPC, and is the control plane access in our network only?
03:27 Sofia: we offer a private deployment option where control plane endpoints are reachable only from your VPC (private link/VPC peering options), and you can choose on-prem package for air-gapped infra. for most banks the private control plane plus customer-managed keys is enough.
03:40 Maya: great. what about model variants and fallbacks — if a GPU pool is saturated we need graceful degradation rather than hard errors.
03:50 Ethan: we have smart routing — policy-based routing by latency/cost/region. you can configure automatic fallbacks to a compatible lower-cost or quantized variant. we'll log those fallbacks and you can set alerts.
04:05 Connor: can you support pinned model versions? we want to test a rollout on a subset of traffic.
04:10 Ethan: yes — rollouts, canary, A/B, and automatic rollback on quality regressions are supported in the Console.
04:18 Maya: for compliance we need SOC2 Type II evidence and ISO docs, and also network diagrams for our auditors.
04:25 Sofia: we'll send the SOC2 and ISO PDFs plus the private deployment architecture diagram. note that for HSM integration there's extra setup, we'll loop in our infra ops.
04:37 Aisha: encryption at rest — can Redwood use our KMS for model artifacts and prefixes?
04:42 Ethan: yes, customer-managed KMS for keys; HSM options available for private deployments.
04:48 Maya: curious on cost assumptions — what's the per-token unit cost delta between hosted and dedicated?
04:54 Sofia: dedicated pricing is a mix of committed monthly for the reserved GPUs plus a lower per-token execution cost. bursts from shared pools are priced higher. i'll include an example pricing spreadsheet showing unit economics comparing the two.
05:10 Connor: do you support mixed workloads on the same GPU pool — e.g., chat plus batch embedding?
05:17 Ethan: we recommend isolating heavy batch embedding onto separate pools or scheduling them in off-peak windows; mixing is possible but can impact tail latency. we have autoscale and QoS rules to prioritize latency-sensitive routes.
05:30 Maya: for benchmarking, what do you need from us?
05:35 Ethan: a sample prompt set, representative input sizes, and traffic shape (concurrent sessions, peak qps). for embeddings we need a subset of documents or a synthetic dataset and target batch size. we'll run a benchmark on a dedicated test pool and share latency/throughput profiles.
05:50 Sofia: action plan — we'll size an initial config for you, propose committed capacity tiers, share security docs, and schedule the benchmark.
05:58 Aisha: one last thing — we use strict IP allow lists and SSO via SAML. any blockers?
06:04 Ethan: no blockers; SAML SSO is supported and IP allow lists + VPC peering are standard for private deployments.
06:12 Connor: is there an SLA for p95 latency?
06:16 Sofia: our Dedicated offering has uptime SLAs and we can contract latency targets for enterprise deals, we typically measure by route/model and can include latency SLOs in the agreement.
06:27 Maya: timeline — we'd like to pilot in July and make a procurement decision by end of July.
06:33 Sofia: that works. we'll aim to have pricing and docs to you by Wednesday and slot a benchmark run the week of 6/22 as proposed.
06:42 Ethan: i'll follow up with a proposed config and the steps for the benchmark, including what logs/metrics we'll provide.
06:48 Sofia: thank you all — wrap up quick recap of next steps.
06:52 Maya: thanks.
